newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Analysts unimpressed by Manila property firms' net.
newsitem.headline: Analysts unimpressed by Manila property firms' net.

text.p: Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc and its subsidiary Empire East Land Holdings Inc on Wednesday unveiled double-digit growth rates for their first quarter net profits, but analysts were unimpressed.
Dismissing rumours of a financial crisis in the company, Megaworld said it posted a 14 percent growth in net income in the first three months of the year to reach 419 million pesos.
Megaworld said its mass housing development unit Empire East registered a 16 percent growth in net profit to 349.2 million pesos.
"The first quarter results should reassure investors about the healthy financial state of the Megaworld group," corporate secretary Cirilo Manlangit said in a statement.
"But it's not impressive. Ayala Land posted a 15 percent growth, and it did not erase the fears," an analyst at a foreign brokerage house said. Ayala Land is the industry leader.
"I don't think it will calm the market," he added.
The Philippine property sector has been hit by heavy selldown since the start of the month on fears that property prices were set to crash as a result of excess supplies.
Megaworld and Empire East took the worst beating, falling near their book value levels in the past days.
Megaworld said its cash position improved by 319 percent during the period to 3.9 billion pesos from 938.5 million pesos in the same period last year.

Rachel Evangelista, a property analyst of All AsiaCapital and Trust Corp, said the growth rates were not high enough to stop the talk since other similarly positioned property companies have not released their earning figures yet.
Although, she said, the rumour had been sidelined as investors had to grapple with new market concerns such as a slowdown in corporate earnings especially from blue chip companies.
Any recovery in the coming days would be due to technical buying and not on renewed confidence on the property sector, she said.
Megaworld lost 20 centavos on Wednesday to 5.90 pesos, while Empire East shed 10 centavos to 4.90 pesos.
